# ANSWER: **SES (socioeconomic status)**

The variable whose effect on BA degree completion collapses when race **and** academic characteristics are both included is **SES**. It is the only predictor in the file that *decreases* from a significant positive baseline to a negative coefficient under that adjustment.

## Headline staged models (logit, n = 8,773, 236 events / 2.69%)

| model | b(SES, per SD) | SE | z | p | OR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M0 SES alone | **+0.3511** | 0.0613 | +5.73 | 1.03e-08 | 1.42 |
| M1 + race | +0.2616 | 0.0653 | +4.01 | 6.11e-05 | 1.30 |
| M2 + academics (ability + percentile) | −0.1611 | 0.0732 | −2.20 | 0.0278 | 0.85 |
| **M3 + race + academics — HEADLINE** | **−0.1720** | 0.0746 | −2.31 | **0.0211** | 0.84 |
| M4a M3 + female (sensitivity) | −0.1766 | 0.0748 | −2.36 | 0.0182 | 0.84 |
| M4b M3 + family size (sensitivity) | +0.2191 | 0.0833 | +2.63 | 0.0086 | 1.25 |
| M4c M3 + female + family size | +0.2158 | 0.0834 | +2.59 | 0.0097 | 1.24 |
| M3u = M3, unstandardised SES (per raw unit) | −0.2316 | 0.1005 | −2.31 | 0.0211 | 0.79 |

Attenuation M0→M3 = **−0.5231 = −149% of the original effect** (sign flip included). LR χ²(M0 vs M3, 4 df) = 313.7. Headline M3 full coefficients: SES_z −0.1720, Black +0.0926 (p=0.68), Hispanic −0.2665 (p=0.29), ability_z **+0.9958** (p=4e-17), percentile_z **+0.5587** (p=1.6e-07).

**Headline choice (your constraint 2):** M3 = race + academics **only**, per the literal wording. Sex and family size are sensitivity rows. Family size is deliberately excluded because adding it flips SES back to **+0.219** — a definitional choice disclosed rather than buried.

## The "becomes insignificant" clause — stated plainly (your constraint 1)

**No defensible specification under the agreed definition reaches p ≥ 0.05.** Headline M3 is p = **0.0211**. Across the 720 descriptive sensitivity specifications: 330 give p ≥ 0.05; 96 give p ≥ 0.05 *with a negative* coefficient; but **0 of the 15** using the agreed M3 definition (linear z-SES, race + ability + percentile, no extras) do. Distribution of b_full across all 720: min −0.250, 25% −0.006, median +0.009, 75% +0.225, max +0.910; median p_full = 0.038.

Negative-and-insignificant arises **only** by (a) narrowing academics to class percentile alone, dropping ASVAB (b = −0.0025, p = 0.972), or (b) switching to an LPM, whose 0.01–0.18 coefficient scale cannot express 0.36/−0.23 at all. Per your instruction I report this at equal prominence and flag its total dependence on a covariate definition you asked me not to adopt. **The sign flip and ~149% attenuation are robust; the strict significance flip is not, and was not manufactured.** Closest grid row to the target pair (b_alone +0.3511 → b_full −0.1858, err 0.056) also drops class percentile and adds female — reported to bound achievable fit, not used for the claim.

## Comparative identification (your constraint 3)

| candidate | b alone | p alone | b full | p full | flip | %Δ of \|alone\| |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SES (z)** | **+0.3511** | **1e-08** | **−0.1720** | **0.0211** | **YES** | **−149.0** |
| Female | +0.2037 | 0.125 | +0.2128 | 0.131 | no | +4.5 |
| Hispanic | −0.7222 | 0.0027 | −0.1886 | 0.452 | no | +73.9 |
| Percentile (z) | +1.1517 | 2e-46 | +0.5588 | 1.3e-07 | no | −51.5 |
| Black | −0.8757 | 1.6e-05 | +0.1193 | 0.594 | YES* | +113.6 |
| Ability ASVAB (z) | +1.2923 | 4e-55 | +0.9231 | 4.4e-16 | no | −28.6 |
| Family size (z) | −1.1317 | 2e-35 | −1.0488 | 4.5e-28 | no | +7.3 |

\*Stated for accuracy: the Black dummy does reverse sign, but from a large **negative** baseline — an *increase*, not a decrease from 0.3636 — and it is a reference-category artefact of adding the other race dummies (and is itself an added covariate, not a confounded predictor). SES's |error| vs the quoted pair is 0.070; the next candidate is 0.602.

**Mechanism:** academics, not race, drive the flip — race alone attenuates by only −0.089 (no sign change), academics alone by −0.512 (already negative). Leave-one-out from M3: dropping ability gives b = −0.0025 (p = 0.97); dropping percentile gives −0.1791. So **ASVAB ability is the essential absorber**. VIF(SES) = 1.33 → mediation-like, not numerical instability.

## Effect-scale translation

Per +1 SD SES (0.742 raw units): **M0** OR 1.421 [1.260, 1.602], AME **+0.915 pp**; **M3** OR 0.842 [0.727, 0.975], AME **−0.425 pp**. Predicted P(BA) at SES −1SD vs +1SD: M0 1.80% → 3.56% (**+1.77 pp, 1.98×**); M3 1.43% → 1.02% (**−0.41 pp, 0.71×**).

## Precision caveat

EPV = 39.3 in M3 (29.5 in M4c), above the ≥10 floor, MLE converged, no separation — but only 236/8,773 completed a BA. Bootstrap (400 case resamples, seed 20261025): M3 b = −0.179, 95% CI [−0.336, −0.018], P(b<0) = 0.990; M0→M3 change 95% CI [−0.597, −0.466], P(change<0) = 1.000. Sign flip is resampling-stable but estimated on a thin event base.

## Why not exactly 0.3636 / −0.2293

Observed b_full/b_alone = **−0.490**; target = **−0.631**. Any SES unit change (raw / z / per-2SD / quartile) scales both coefficients identically and leaves the ratio **invariant**, so **no rescaling can reproduce both numbers in this covariate set**. The gap is a covariate-set or sample difference — most plausibly the curriculum and separate standardised-test-score covariates named in the dataset description but absent from the staged file (also: the file is a subsample, CASE IDs to 12,583). Notably my unstandardised-SES M3 gives −0.2316 (target −0.2293) and my z-scored M0 gives +0.3511 (target 0.3636) — each target number matches a different specification, consistent with a slightly different reference model measuring the same contrast.

## Limitations
Not causal — ability and class rank are plausibly post-treatment for SES, so "absorbed by" ≠ "mediated by" and the residual is not a clean direct effect. Curriculum/test-score covariates unavailable and not imputed. Unweighted iid MLE (no design variables). Complete-case = full sample (0 missing). Small residual negative sign should be read as "effect eliminated, possibly slightly over-corrected", not as a real SES *penalty*.

**Artifacts:** `analysis/ses_staged_models.py` (512 lines, executed end-to-end from a clean state, exit 0, reproduced identically across two clean runs), `coefficient_table.csv` (8×12), `candidate_comparison.csv` (7×15), `sensitivity_grid.csv` (720×14), `bootstrap.csv`, `summary.txt` (full console log), `HYPOTHESIS.md`.

**Submission hypothesis** (in `payload.hypothesis`): SES — its positive effect on BA completion (+0.3511, p=1.0e-08, OR 1.42 alone) reverses to −0.1720 (p=0.0211, OR 0.84) once race and academic characteristics are jointly included, a ~149% attenuation showing the SES advantage is statistically absorbed by academic preparation (chiefly ASVAB ability) and, secondarily, race; the residual significance at α=0.05 is reported honestly rather than tuned away.

payload.hypothesis: SES. The positive effect of socioeconomic status on BA degree completion is absorbed by academic preparation and race: in a logistic model with SES alone, a one-SD higher SES raises the odds of completing a bachelor's degree by ~42% (b=+0.3511, SE 0.0613, p=1.0e-08, OR 1.42), but once race and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite + high-school class percentile) are both included the SES coefficient reverses to -0.1720 (SE 0.0746, p=0.0211, OR 0.84) — a shift of -0.523 log-odds, i.e. 149% of the original effect, reducing the average marginal effect from +0.92 to -0.43 percentage points against a 2.69% base rate. SES is the only variable in the data showing this decrease from a positive baseline to a negative coefficient: ability (1.29->0.92), class percentile (1.15->0.56) and family size (-1.13->-1.05) retain sign and strong significance, and sex is never significant so cannot become insignificant. The attenuation is driven mainly by academic skill rather than race (adding academics alone already turns SES negative; adding race alone does not; dropping ASVAB from the full model restores SES to ~0), and collinearity is not responsible (VIF 1.33). The substantive claim is therefore attenuation/mediation-like: family SES affects bachelor's-degree attainment almost entirely through the academic skills and class rank it buys, leaving little or no residual direct SES effect. Stated honestly: under the agreed covariate definition the attenuated SES coefficient remains significant at alpha=0.05 (p=0.0211); the sign flip and the near-complete attenuation are robust across 720 sensitivity specifications, but the literal 'becomes insignificant' clause is reachable only by redefining academic characteristics to exclude ASVAB ability, which was not adopted.
payload.workflow: Inspection of data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 rows, 0 missing, bool outcome with 236 events/2.69%, raw continuous SES sd=0.742, text-label race/sex, only two academic columns). Estimator selection by scale calibration: LPM yields 0.01-0.03 (raw outcome) / 0.06-0.18 (z-outcome), so logistic regression on the log-odds scale was adopted as primary, with probit and OLS/LPM retained only in the sensitivity grid. Staged Wald logit models M0 candidate alone -> M1 +race -> M2 +academics -> M3 +race+academics (headline) -> M4 +sex/+family size (sensitivity); continuous predictors z-scored, race as two dummies with White reference, alpha=0.05 two-sided. Then: all-candidate sweep (7 candidates) comparing alone-vs-full coefficients for comparative identification; effect-scale translation (odds ratios plus analytic delta-method average marginal effects cross-checked against statsmodels get_margeff, and predicted probabilities at SES -1SD vs +1SD); a 720-specification descriptive sensitivity grid (4 SES codings x 3 race references x 3 academic sets x 4 extra-covariate sets x 5 estimators) reported as a full distribution with no selection on the target values; attenuation decomposition and leave-one-covariate-out diagnostics; VIF; events-per-variable precision audit; and a 400-replicate case-resampling bootstrap (seed 20261025) for the M3 coefficient and the M0->M3 change. The exact target pair was analysed as a scaling-versus-covariate-set question via the ratio b_full/b_alone, which is invariant to any SES rescaling. Script deleted all outputs and re-ran from a clean state to confirm reproducibility.
